title: Cycling and the City
text:
A recent report published by the city council shows that cycling to work has increased by nearly a fifth over the past three years. The authors attribute this growth mainly to the construction of protected bike lanes in the city centre. Researchers also noted that most new cyclists are people aged between 25 and 40 who previously relied on buses. However, the report warns that accidents still occur frequently at busy junctions.

Local business owners have responded to the findings with mixed feelings. Some argue that fewer parking spaces have made it harder for customers to reach their shops. Others claim that cyclists spend more money locally than drivers, because they stop more often. The council plans to review parking policies next spring, after a shoppers' survey due in January.

questions.text: According to the report, by how much has cycling to work increased over the past three years?
What do some local business owners argue?
options: Cyclists spend more money than drivers
Fewer parking spaces make it harder for customers to reach their shops
The council has already changed its parking policies

questions.text: What can be inferred about the new cyclists mentioned in the report?
options: They were mostly people who used to travel by bus
They had never used any form of public transport
They were mostly students living outside the city

questions.text: Why does the council plan to wait for the shoppers' survey before deciding on parking policies?
options: It has already decided to remove all parking spaces
It wants evidence about shoppers' habits before making changes
The law requires the survey to be published in spring
It is waiting for the accident figures to be published

paragraph_translations: Un informe reciente publicado por el ayuntamiento muestra que el uso de la bicicleta para ir al trabajo ha aumentado casi un veinte por ciento en los últimos tres años. Los autores atribuyen este crecimiento principalmente a la construcción de carriles bici protegidos en el centro de la ciudad. Los investigadores también señalaron que la mayoría de los nuevos ciclistas son personas de entre 25 y 40 años que antes utilizaban el autobús. Sin embargo, el informe advierte de que los accidentes siguen ocurriendo con frecuencia en los cruces más transitados.

Los propietarios de negocios locales han reaccionado a las conclusiones con sentimientos encontrados. Algunos sostienen que la reducción de plazas de aparcamiento ha dificultado que los clientes lleguen a sus tiendas. Otros afirman que los ciclistas gastan más dinero en la zona que los conductores, porque se detienen con más frecuencia. El ayuntamiento prevé revisar las políticas de aparcamiento la próxima primavera, tras una encuesta a los compradores prevista para enero.
